why: The simplest grid DP: a cell can only be entered from above or from the left, so the number of paths to it is the sum of the paths to those two cells.
hints: Think about the last move into the bottom-right cell. Where could you have been just before?
ways[r][c] = ways[r-1][c] + ways[r][c-1], with every cell of the first row and first column equal to 1.
Keep one row of length n and update it left to right m - 1 times: row[c] += row[c-1]. O(m * n). (The closed form C(m+n-2, m-1) also works.)
pitfalls: A single row or a single column has exactly one path.
The answer can exceed 32 bits for 20 x 20 grids in other languages.
